reaction: It is satisfying to see how one rising follower can move both wings.
reason: The chapter asks for a wave with the original cam first, and the removable handle should turn it.

reaction: The keeper pin and shaft exchange were more involved than I expected.

effect: The comparison confirmed that the two-humped cam gives two waves per turn, completing the dragon.
reaction: The wave-wave pattern made the cam comparison satisfying and easy to understand.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the wing rods was most worthwhile: it showed how one follower can move two hinged wings while the body stays still.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the rods on the unmounted dragon was the least worthwhile moment; the required mounting order was not clear beforehand.

surprise.text: The cam exchange involved a keeper pin and withdrawing the shaft, more than simply swapping discs.

arbitrary.text: The rods’ inability to connect before mounting initially felt arbitrary, although mounting the body first made the order more understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: comparing the cams made the mechanism understandable, and Jo’s unfinished fair drawing made me curious about what comes next.
